MODULE 6: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-2 CONSTRAINED SPACE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of three. The offense will start in the midrange or outside the 3PT line. One defender is allowed to play defense anywhere outside the paint, while the other can only play defense anywhere inside the paint. The offense will check the ball with the first defender, cueing the live 1-on-2. The offense has an eight second shot clock to score inside the paint.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing ball manipulation skills
- Creating space and advantage from a neutral position
- Creative finishing

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense can only use one hand.
- One defender can play anywhere, while the other defender can only play inside or outside the paint.
- The offensive player can only score at the rim.
- Add a second offensive player to play 2-on-2 with the same spatial loads on the defense.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure defenders remain in their areas.
- Count down from eight seconds.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Where was the space?
- What did you see on that rep?
- How else could you get your shot off?

Load for younger players

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 3-ON-3 DEFENSIVE SHUTDOWN

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of three. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams per basket and a maximum of six. Teams will play continuous half-court 3-on-3 with additional teams waiting at the half-court area. If a defensive stop is secured (defensive rebound or forced turnover), the defense gets 2 points and stays on defense while a new offense comes on from the half-court area (the old offense team rotates off to the end of the line). If the offense scores, they rotate to defense and play against a new team on offense (the old defense team rotates off to the end of the line).

#### SCORING

Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Preventing straight line drives
- Rotating on defense
- Helping and stopping the ball
- Finishing possessions with defensive rebound

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the defense can only play with one hand if the offense finds the activity too challenging.
- The defense must always ensure there is adequate ball pressure. The on-ball defender must be within arm distance from the offensive player.
- The defense must prevent all baseline drives.
- The defense must prevent all offensive rebounds.
- The defense must avoid fouling.
- Instead of the offense starting at halfcourt, an offensive player must inbound the ball from a sideline out-of-bounds. The other two offensive players must cut to get open.
- Incorporate half-court shot clock (24 seconds) and shot clock reset (14 seconds).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure defender is within arm distance of the ball-handler.
- Officiate loads.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- What does good ball pressure look like?
- How can we keep good spacing on offense to make it harder for the defense?

GAME TIME

### SHOOTING COMPETITIONS

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players will shoot with two balls in groups of four or five players. The first team to score five catch-and-shoot shots from four different random spots wins. As soon as one team scores five shots, they move to the next spot. The shooting location must be in the mid-range or 3PT based on the age and ability of the players.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Swishes are counted as two baskets instead of one.
- One player from each team can play as a defender guarding another team. The offensive players must create separation to score against this defender.
- Play to three baskets instead of five. Change defenders each time a team completes a spot.

#### SCORING

First team to 5 baskets from each spot wins 1 point. First team to 4 points wins.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players shoot from random spots.
- Encourage players to use their leadership voice to keep count.
- Encourage players to shoot with proper technique.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Aiming for the back of the rim

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

N/A

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED HALF-COURT

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining excellent spacing
- Looking to contain defensive match-ups 1-on-1

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you get the most efficient shot?
- How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?
- What can you do to space the floor effectively?

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the lava load), ready to receive the ball.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!
